title: Supported finite torsion layers of a divisible-sheaf injective resolution
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], with open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Use ordinary small-etale module sheaves and derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Fix a prime $\ell$ and an abelian sheaf $M$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ such that multiplication by $\ell$ is an epimorphism of sheaves. Let $M[0]\to I^\bullet$ be any injective resolution in abelian sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$. For $r\geq1$ put $A_r=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$, $F_r=\ker(\ell^r:M\to M)$, and define actual subcomplexes
$$J_r^\bullet=\ker(\ell^r:I^\bullet\to I^\bullet),\qquad K_r^\bullet=i^{-1}\ker(J_r^\bullet\to j_*j^{-1}J_r^\bullet),\qquad E_r^\bullet=\Gamma(Z,K_r^\bullet).$$
The supported kernel is [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. The augmentation $F_r[0]\to J_r^\bullet$ is an injective resolution in $A_r$-module sheaves. Every term of $K_r$ is injective over $A_r$, and the natural derived comparison is an isomorphism
$$QK_r\xrightarrow{\sim}i_r^!F_r$$
in $D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A_r)$, for the closed-support adjoint of [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]. For $m\geq0$, sending $1$ to a global cocycle gives a natural isomorphism
$$H^m(E_r)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A_r)}(A_{r,Z},i_r^!F_r[m]).$$
For every $a,b\geq1$, the inclusions and multiplication maps give degreewise short exact sequences
$$0\to J_a\xrightarrow{\mathrm{incl}}J_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\ell^a}J_b\to0,\qquad 0\to K_a\xrightarrow{\mathrm{incl}}K_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\ell^a}K_b\to0,\qquad 0\to E_a\xrightarrow{\mathrm{incl}}E_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\ell^a}E_b\to0.$$
The first two are sequences of $A_{a+b}$-module complexes with restricted outer scalars. For $N\geq r$, the map $K_N\to K_r$ is multiplication by $\ell^{N-r}$, and $K_r\to K_N$ is inclusion; the same holds for $J$ and $E$. Under the displayed comparisons these are the maps induced by $F_N\xrightarrow{\ell^{N-r}}F_r$ and $F_r\hookrightarrow F_N$. More precisely, the comparisons identify the scalar restriction of $QK_r$ to $A_N$ with $i_N^!(\operatorname{Res}_{A_N\to A_r}F_r)$, agree with the comparison at $r=N$, and identify the displayed short exact coefficient rows with the derived closed-support images of the corresponding rows of the $F_r$. These identifications respect composition of coefficient maps and the closed-adjunction counits.

source.place: Tag 0DD7 (lemma-torsion), first paragraph: injective abelian sheaves are divisible on sections; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), supported adjunction and preservation of injectives. Agent-derived finite torsion-layer refinement of these facts, used in place of the Godement model in ILO Expose XVI Proposition 3.3.2, printed p.245.

proof.text: Sectionwise divisibility. If $T$ is an injective abelian sheaf and $V$ is an object of its site, represent $s\in T(V)$ by $f:\mathbf Z[V]\to T$ using [lem-trf-site-free-sheaf-sections]. Multiplication by a positive integer $n$ is monic on the free abelian presheaf on $V$: in each free basis its kernel consists of integer coefficients $c$ with $nc=0$, hence $c=0$. It remains monic after sheafification by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends $f$ along this monomorphism to $h:\mathbf Z[V]\to T$ with $h\circ n=f$. The section corresponding to $h$ has $n$ times itself equal to $s$. Thus $T(V)$ is divisible, in particular for $V=X$ or $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, first paragraph; finite-exponent refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: The torsion complexes resolve the torsion sheaves. Step 1 gives the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to J_r\to I\xrightarrow{\ell^r}I\to0$. Since $H^0(I)=M$, $H^q(I)=0$ for $q\ne0$, and $\ell^r:M\to M$ is epic (compose the given epimorphism $r$ times), the long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] gives $H^0(J_r)=F_r$ and $H^q(J_r)=0$ for $q\ne0$. The identification in degree zero is precisely the kernel augmentation. For injectivity over $A_r$, let $B\hookrightarrow C$ be a monomorphism of $A_r$-module sheaves and $B\to I^q[\ell^r]$ a map. Forget the scalars and extend its composite $B\to I^q$ to $C\to I^q$ by injectivity. Since $\ell^r C=0$, the extension lands in the kernel $I^q[\ell^r]$ and is $A_r$-linear (an additive map between sheaves killed by $\ell^r$ commutes with integer scalars). This proves that $F_r[0]\to J_r$ is an injective resolution over $A_r$.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, first paragraph; finite-exponent refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: Supported terms. Write $H(T)=i^{-1}\ker(T\to j_*j^{-1}T)$ and put $T^q=H(I^q)$. By [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction], $i_*$ is exact on abelian sheaves and left adjoint to $H$. Hence for a monomorphism $G'\hookrightarrow G$ of abelian sheaves on $Z$, the map $i_*G'\to i_*G$ is a monomorphism, and the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(G,T^q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*G,I^q)$ turn the surjective restriction for the injective $I^q$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] into surjectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(G,T^q)\to\operatorname{Hom}_Z(G',T^q)$. Thus $T^q$ is an injective abelian sheaf on $Z$ (the proof of Stacks 09XQ). Sectionwise kernels [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and exactness of $i^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] identify $H(I^q[\ell^r])$ with $H(I^q)[\ell^r]$: both kernels first impose support on $Z$ and then impose $\ell^r=0$, in either order. Hence $K_r^q=T^q[\ell^r]$, compatibly with differentials and inclusions. The extension argument of step 2, now on $Z$ with target $T^q$, proves that $K_r^q$ is injective over $A_r$.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, support adjunction and its derived functor; finite-coefficient refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: The fixed-ring comparison. The category of $A_r$-module sheaves has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](2) to $H$ and the resolution in step 2. It gives the natural isomorphism $QH(J_r)\simeq RH(F_r[0])$. The adjoint in [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction] is this right derived supported functor, with the support-inclusion counit. Consequently this is the required $QK_r\simeq i_r^!F_r$. In particular its counit is induced by $i_*K_r\to J_r$ and the augmentation $F_r[0]\to J_r$.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, support adjunction and its derived functor; finite-coefficient refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: Cocycles and derived morphisms. Since $K_r$ is bounded below and termwise injective, [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identify maps $A_{r,Z}[0]\to QK_r[m]$ in $D$ with chain maps modulo chain homotopy. The free-module universal property [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property], for the terminal sheaf of sets and coefficient sheaf $A_{r,Z}$, identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A_{r,Z},K_r^q)$ with $\Gamma(Z,K_r^q)$ by evaluation at $1$. A chain map from $A_{r,Z}[0]$ to $K_r[m]$ is therefore a global degree-$m$ cocycle. A chain homotopy changes it by a boundary (the possible shift sign has the same image subgroup). Taking the quotient gives $H^m(E_r)$ and the asserted isomorphism, with inverse given by sending $1$ to a representative cocycle. Compose with step 4 to obtain the displayed target. All identifications commute with chain maps.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, support adjunction and its derived functor; finite-coefficient refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: Exact coefficient rows. For any divisible abelian group $D$ and $a,b\geq1$, the kernel of $\ell^a:D[\ell^{a+b}]\to D[\ell^b]$ is $D[\ell^a]$. Given $y\in D[\ell^b]$, choose $x\in D$ with $\ell^ax=y$; then $\ell^{a+b}x=\ell^by=0$. Thus this row is short exact. Apply this calculation to the divisible groups $I^q(V)$ from step 1, for every etale $V\to X$, to obtain the $J$ row. Apply it to $T^q(V)$ for every etale $V\to Z$, with $T^q$ injective by step 3, to obtain the $K$ row. Finally apply it to $T^q(Z)$ and use $E_r^q=\Gamma(Z,T^q[\ell^r])=T^q(Z)[\ell^r]$ (kernels of sheaves are sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]) to obtain the $E$ row. All maps commute with differentials because they are integer multiplications or inclusions of their kernels. These are $A_{a+b}$-linear rows after scalar restriction. This proves surjectivity on supported sections directly, without applying a nonexact functor to a short exact row.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, first paragraph; finite-exponent refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: The sheaf coefficient rows themselves are short exact. The same kernel calculation as in step 6 applies locally to $M$: given $y\in F_b(V)$, local surjectivity of $\ell^a:M\to M$ supplies a covering and lifts $x$ with $\ell^ax=y$; each lift lies in $F_{a+b}$ since $\ell^{a+b}x=0$. Here local surjectivity is exactly the sheaf-epimorphism criterion [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]. Thus $0\to F_a\to F_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\ell^a}F_b\to0$ is short exact. The kernel augmentations give a commuting diagram from this row, concentrated in degree zero, to the $J$ row of step 6. Both vertical inclusions and multiplication maps are literally restrictions of those on $M\to I$.

source.place: Tag 0DD7, lemma-torsion, first paragraph; finite-exponent refinement written by Q56.

proof.text: Restriction of coefficients. Fix $N\geq r$; restriction $\operatorname{Res}$ along $A_N\to A_r$ keeps underlying abelian sheaves, so it is exact and commutes with $H$ and $\Gamma$. On $A_N$-module sheaves $H$ is additive and left exact (a kernel followed by the exact $i^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]); with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] its derived functors $R^pH$ over $A_N$ vanish on injectives for $p>0$ and have long exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]. Claim: for all $q$ and $1\leq s\leq N$ the $A_N$-sheaf $J_s^q=I^q[\ell^s]$ is $H$-acyclic over $A_N$. For $s=N$ it is injective over $A_N$ by step 2. For $s<N$, step 6 with $a=s$, $b=N-s$ gives the short exact sequence $0\to J_s^q\to J_N^q\xrightarrow{\ell^s}J_{N-s}^q\to0$ of $A_N$-sheaves. By step 3, $H$ sends its last map to $\ell^s:T^q[\ell^N]\to T^q[\ell^{N-s}]$, an epimorphism by the $K$ row of step 6. The long exact sequence and $R^pH(J_N^q)=0$ for $p>0$ give $R^1H(J_s^q)=0$ and $R^{p+1}H(J_s^q)\cong R^pH(J_{N-s}^q)$ for $p\geq1$. Induction on $p$, for all $1\leq t\leq N$ at once, proves the claim. Hence $\operatorname{Res}F_r[0]\to\operatorname{Res}J_r$ is a bounded-below resolution by $H$-acyclic $A_N$-sheaves, and [sk-thm-acyclicity] makes the canonical comparison $\alpha$ of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] an isomorphism $Q\operatorname{Res}K_r=QH(\operatorname{Res}J_r)\simeq i_N^!(\operatorname{Res}F_r)$, $i_N^!$ being this derived supported functor by [def-per-closed-support-plus-adjunction]. Together with step 4 this gives $\operatorname{Res}(i_r^!F_r)\simeq\operatorname{Res}QK_r\simeq i_N^!(\operatorname{Res}F_r)$. Both comparisons are induced by the same support inclusion $i_*K_r\to J_r$ and augmentation, so they respect the closed-adjunction counits; for $r=N$ the restriction is the identity and this is step 4. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives naturality in chain maps of such resolutions.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic, and the derived functor of sections with support defined after it; dimension shifting along the torsion rows, written by Q56 in place of the Godement coefficient compatibility of ILO XVI Proposition 3.3.2, printed p.245.

proof.text: Maps and rows in a common coefficient category. Fix $N$ and regard all $J_s,K_s$ for $s\leq N$ as $A_N$-complexes. Step 8 makes their supported comparisons natural in their chain maps, even though the restricted $J_s$ need only be support-acyclic. For $N\geq r$ the maps on $J$ are the kernel inclusion and multiplication by $\ell^{N-r}$, lifting exactly $F_r\hookrightarrow F_N$ and $F_N\xrightarrow{\ell^{N-r}}F_r$. Applying $H$ and then $\Gamma$ gives the asserted $K$ and $E$ maps. For a coefficient row set $N=a+b$. The augmentation diagram of step 7 is a morphism of degreewise short exact rows. Its associated distinguished triangles and their connecting maps are natural by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. To check the connecting arrow as well, use the usual cone of $J_a\to J_{a+b}$. Its terms are finite sums of support-acyclic terms, and $H$ is additive, so applying $H$ to this cone gives the cone of $K_a\to K_{a+b}$. The cone-to-$J_b$ quasi-isomorphism becomes an isomorphism after deriving $H$; [sk-thm-acyclicity] identifies this map with the cone-to-$K_b$ map. This identifies the entire $K$ triangle, including its connecting arrow, with the derived supported coefficient triangle. The cocycle identifications of step 5 give the corresponding $E$ maps. Finally, successive inclusions compose as inclusions, successive reductions multiply as $\ell^{N-s}\ell^{s-r}=\ell^{N-r}$, and any composite of the coefficient chain maps is sent to its composite by $H$ and $\Gamma$. Naturality in step 8 therefore gives composition compatibility. The support inclusions commute with every one of these maps, which gives precisely the asserted compatibility with closed-adjunction counits.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 3.3.2, printed p.245: coefficient-compatible supported models. The injective torsion-layer refinement is written by Q56 using Stacks Tags 0DD7 and 09XQ.

tool_uses.why: Steps 3 and 8 use exact inverse image only to move the torsion kernel through i inverse image and to see that the supported functor is left exact. The perverse unit does not supply this general site-functor property.

Steps 4 and 8 check the enough-injectives hypothesis of the right-derived comparison and of the derived long exact sequence for ordinary finite-coefficient sheaves. This is categorical infrastructure for the prescribed supported model.
Step 5 uses the free-module universal property at the terminal sheaf to identify Hom from the constant rank-one module with global sections. No trace-formula argument is used.

Steps 8 and 9 need the canonical derived comparison on bounded-below support-acyclic resolutions after scalar restriction. This generic acyclic-resolution theorem replaces no step of the perverse unit.

Step 3 uses the abelian support adjunction i_* -| i^!_0 with exact i_* to see that supported kernels of injective abelian sheaves are injective (Stacks 09XQ). The perverse unit has no own node for this ordinary adjunction.
Step 8 uses the long exact sequence of right derived functors for the dimension shift proving support-acyclicity of the restricted torsion layers. Generic homological algebra.
